{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Check for duplicate patient_id values
print("Number of unique patient_id values:", df['patient_id'].nunique())
print("Total number of rows:", len(df))
print("Number of duplicate patient_id values:", len(df) - df['patient_id'].nunique())

# Check the sample_seq for each patient
df_grouped = df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].max().reset_index()
print("\nMax sample_seq per patient:")
print(df_grouped['sample_seq'].describe())

# Identify patients with multiple sample_seq entries
duplicates = df_grouped[df_grouped['sample_seq'] > 1]
print(f"\nNumber of patients with multiple sample_seq entries (re-tested): {len(duplicates)}")

# Confirm that the highest sample_seq row is the one to keep
# For each patient, check if the max sample_seq matches the row with highest sample_seq
max_sample_seq_per_patient = df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].max()

# Create a boolean mask for the highest sample_seq row per patient
keep_rows = df.set_index('patient_id')['sample_seq'].map(max_sample_seq_per_patient) == df['sample_seq']

# Verify that this keeps exactly one row per patient
print(f"\nNumber of rows after deduplication (keeping highest sample_seq per patient): {keep_rows.sum()}")

# Keep only the highest sample_seq rows per patient
df_dedup = df[keep_rows].copy()
print(f"\nFinal dataset shape after deduplication: {df_dedup.shape}")"}
